newsitem.title: USA: RJR, Philip Morris bonds widen after S&P action.
newsitem.headline: RJR, Philip Morris bonds widen after S&P action.

text.p: Bonds of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp and Philip Morris Cos Inc widened five basis points after news hit the Street of a potential downgrade to the tobacco firms' ratings, traders said.
"Tobacco bonds widened five basis points across the board after the ratings news," said one high-grade trader.
Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it may cut the ratings of tobacco companies with U.S. litigation exposure.
Among the firms mentioned by S&P were RJR Nabisco, Philip Morris, Loews Corp and B.A.T Industries PLC.
RJR 8-3/4 percent paper due 2005 widened to 200 basis points, while Philip Morris' debt due 2007 widened from 85 to 90 basis points, traders said.
Market players reacted with surprise as speculation by participants was that the potential settlement would be viewed as a long-term positive for the industry.
"People were surprised that this rating came out now," said one high-grade trader. "There's still no agreement yet."
Philip Morris senior unsecured debt is currently rated single-A, while RJR Nabisco's senior unsecured debt is rated BBB-minus by S&P.
Philip Morris stock ended the trading day off 1-5/8 at 41-5/8 while RJR Nabisco stock fell 3/4 to close at 32-3/4.
